subject: Reserve commitment discussion: SKU rebalancing options for Nebula Labs
messages:
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Simon Fletcher <simon.fletcher@nebulalabs.com>
Date: 2028-08-12T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Reserve commitment — initial SKU rebalancing options for Nebula Labs

Irene / Marissa — looping you in as we scope the reserve commitment for Nebula Labs (NEB-9832). Simon shared their usage snapshot (attached) and a rough 12-month forecast: steady daytime QPS, occasional bursts for batch re-ingestion and long-context inference. Key ask from the customer is predictable latency and a simple procurement footprint.

Quick notes from my read of the numbers: 
- Memory/long-context tasks look to be ~10% of requests but dominate tail latency.
- Bulk of traffic is short-turnaround classification/embeddings.

Options to propose to customer: 
1) H100-heavy reserve: best tail-latency and long-context headroom, higher $/GPU but fewer units for memory-heavy jobs.
2) A100-mix reserve: balanced memory vs throughput, easier ops and lower unit cost for steady throughput.
3) L4 as a burst/fallback tier: cost-effective for short contexts and scale-out with cheaper units.

I attached nebula_usage_snapshot.csv and put a preliminary ask for a decision on SKU mix by EOD Aug 18 so procurement can finalize terms. Simon — can you confirm their willingness to sign a 12-month commit vs a 6-month with increasing ramp?

Thanks,
Dev
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Reserve commitment — initial SKU rebalancing options for Nebula Labs

Thanks Dev — appreciate the summary. Two quick asks before we solidify recommendations to procurement: 
- Ben/Marissa: can you run a delta comparing a 12-month fixed commit vs 6-month ramp (same total tokens) showing unit $/token and a tail-latency percentile estimate for each SKU mix?
- Dev: flag any operational constraints for private deployment (VPC tunnel sizing, KV cache sizing) if they pick hybrid SKUs.

Simon — if procurement prefers a single SKU to simplify ordering, we should surface the tradeoffs clearly so they can decide between lower ops complexity vs unit-cost/latency.

Irene
Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Simon Fletcher <simon.fletcher@nebulalabs.com>
Date: 2028-08-14T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Reserve commitment — initial SKU rebalancing options for Nebula Labs

I ran the cost/throughput model (attached: commitment_cost_model.xlsx) and summarized the high-level tradeoffs below. Numbers are illustrative but aligned to our current pricing grid and realistic throughput assumptions.

Summary (12-month, token-normalized):
- Pure H100 commit:
  - Pros: best 99th-tail latency for long-context (<=350ms for their 8k seq jobs), fewer GPUs due to higher memory/compute density.
  - Cons: ~18% higher $/month vs A100 baseline.
- Pure A100 commit:
  - Pros: good throughput for short-context traffic, ~8% lower $/month vs H100 scenario, simpler ops (single SKU).
  - Cons: 99th-tail latency degrades for 8k seq (~600-700ms), may need tiling or KV cache tuning.
- Hybrid (recommended): 60% A100 / 30% H100 / 10% L4 for burst:
  - Pros: balances cost and latency; H100 handles long-context tails; L4 provides cost-effective burst capacity for short-context spikes.
  - Cons: slightly more complex ops (three SKUs), but we can abstract via autoscale groups/policies.

Operational notes:
- Private deployment: need to provision NVLink-friendly nodes for H100; estimated additional network egress tunnel capacity +12% for model warmup traffic on long-context runs.
- Autoscale policy: warm standby of 8-12 H100 slots to prevent cold-start penalties on long-context.

Attachment includes a sensitivity sheet that shows how the $/token moves with 10/20/30% long-context traffic. I put a recommended pricing concession (1 month credit) in the model if Nebraska signs 12-month commit today.

Ben
Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Simon Fletcher <simon.fletcher@nebulalabs.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-08-17T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Reserve commitment — initial SKU rebalancing options for Nebula Labs

Thanks team — useful breakdown. A few items from procurement/ops side at Nebula: 
- Procurement preference: fewer SKUs to simplify purchase orders and forecasting. If we must pick multiple, max 2 SKUs.
- Ops constraint: private deployment with strict network controls; need a clear fallthrough plan if H100 nodes are unavailable during a regional maintenance window.
- Commercial ask: willing to commit to 12 months if we can get a first-month credit and a 10% price hold for any mid-term swap to a different SKU mix.

From my side, the long-context tail is important but it only affects ~8–12% of requests. If a single SKU is required I would prioritize A100 (cost balance) and ask Redwood to guarantee a fallback low-latency path for long-context (e.g., reserved H100 capacity in a secondary region or cached KV path).

Simon
Director, Infrastructure — Nebula Labs
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Simon Fletcher <simon.fletcher@nebulalabs.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-08-20T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Reserve commitment — initial SKU rebalancing options for Nebula Labs

Simon — thanks for the clarity, and appreciate the preference to keep procurement simple. Concluding proposal (for your internal review):

1) Commercial: 12-month commit with first-month credit; 10% price hold on SKU mix swap requests initiated within the first 6 months. (Procurement: we will draft order with a primary SKU and a documented fallback policy.)
2) SKU selection (two-SKU approach to keep procurement simple): Primary = A100 (covers 88–92% of baseline load cost-efficiently), Secondary = H100 (reserved headroom for long-context tails).
3) Ops fallthrough: Redwood will reserve warm H100 capacity in a secondary AZ and provide automatic routing policy to avoid cold starts on long-context requests; KV cache sizing + prewarming script will be in the onboarding checklist.

Attachments: sku_rebalance_playbook.pdf (internal exec summary), commitment_cost_model.xlsx, nebula_usage_snapshot.csv

Next steps:
- Simon: confirm acceptance of the two-SKU approach + commercial ask (first-month credit).
- Redwood: we will prepare PO language and a technical runbook.
- Schedule technical deep-dive: proposed Aug 22 @ 10:00 PDT.

If you confirm, Ben and Dev will prepare the PO and pricing appendix.

Irene
Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference
